extracted.intended_audience: Researchers conducting or reporting health economic evaluations; peer reviewers and journal editors; analysts planning studies; health technology assessment bodies; policy decision‑makers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reporting health economic evaluations so they are clear, transparent, interpretable, and useful for decision-making across health and social contexts. Encapsulates the CHEERS 2022 28‑item checklist and related expectations for stakeholder engagement and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative reporting of costs and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Health economic evaluations compare alternative actions in terms of costs and consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should present both the costs associated with alternatives and their consequences (outcomes) so comparisons can be made; framing should make explicit which alternatives are compared and which cost and consequence items are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to make economic evaluations clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized formats and explicit descriptions so readers (including decision-makers) can understand what was done and why; clarity is a primary aim of the CHEERS update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability and usefulness for decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Make results interpretable and useful for decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present results and uncertainty in ways that enable policy-makers, clinicians, and other stakeholders to make informed choices; contextualize findings relative to decision problems and comparators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the standardized 28‑item checklist (CHEERS 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new 28‑item checklist offers detailed recommendations for reporting economic evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the checklist items when preparing manuscripts and reports; the checklist provides concrete reporting elements to improve completeness, transparency, and reproducibility (the page summarizes the checklist but does not list all items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of methods and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize clarity and transparency in reporting methods and assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly report methods, data sources, model structure, parameter values, and key assumptions so reviewers and readers can evaluate credibility and reproduce or adapt the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate inclusive stakeholder engagement, including patients and the public, in methods and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage relevant stakeholders in design, conduct, interpretation, and reporting to ensure that analyses address important outcomes and perspectives; report how stakeholders influenced the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal applicability across interventions and contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Design guidance to apply universally across various health interventions and contexts (healthcare, public health, education, social care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply checklist principles across settings while adapting specific details to context; ensure reports make clear the setting and scope so readers can judge applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and applicability of evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure economic evaluations are accessible and applicable to a broad range of interventions and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results and limitations clearly so different audiences (researchers, HTA bodies, policy-makers) can assess relevance; include information to support transferability and use in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit for multiple audiences (researchers, reviewers, editors, analysts, HTA bodies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should meet the needs of researchers, peer reviewers, journal editors, analysts planning studies, and health technology assessment bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure reports to satisfy both editorial/review standards (completeness, transparency) and practical decision-making needs (clear presentation of results, uncertainty, and context); consider including elements specifically useful to HTA and policy audiences.
